   "source": [
    "# Time Series - Large Clusters"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "d2315153",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Real station networks can easily hold dozens of series. Showing every station with its own color and label stops working well before that, so the `TimeSeriesCluster` views change their form above a number of series set by `view_specs[\"n_series_max\"]` (10 by default).\n",
    "\n",
    "This tutorial builds a synthetic network of 40 temperature stations to showcase these forms:\n",
    "\n",
    "- Data availability, where the Gantt chart turns into lines\n",
    "- All series in background style, and highlighting a few of them\n",
    "- Correlation between many stations\n",
    "\n",
    "```{seealso}\n",
    "Check out the {doc}`Time Series - Clusters <timeseries_08_cluster>` tutorial first.\n",
    "```"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "515af3e8",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Notebook setup\n",
    "\n",
    "For users running this tutorial as a Jupyter Notebook, this cell must be executed first:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "052d3d2e",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:52:50.033578Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:52:50.032847Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:52:51.296997Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:52:51.295494Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import sys\n",
    "from pathlib import Path\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "\n",
    "# Install `plans` in `google.colab`.\n",
    "# Use `pip install plans` for other environments.\n",
    "\n",
    "if \"google.colab\" in sys.modules:\n",
    "    import os\n",
    "    os.system(f\"{sys.executable} -m pip install -q plans\")\n",
    "\n",
    "from plans.datasets import TemperatureSeries, TemperatureSeriesCluster\n",
    "\n",
    "# This avoids warnings related to uninstalled fonts\n",
    "import logging\n",
    "logging.getLogger('matplotlib.font_manager').setLevel(logging.ERROR)\n",
    "\n",
    "rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=3)  # ensure reproducibility"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "01560f15",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Build a large synthetic network\n",
    "\n",
    "Forty stations are scattered over a 60 x 30 km region. The weather anomalies come from four weather centers, and each station mixes them according to its distance to each center, so nearby stations share more weather. Stations are named from west to east."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "01abcb17",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:52:51.302838Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:52:51.301620Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:52:51.325910Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:52:51.323762Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "n_stations = 40\n",
    "n = 730  # two years, daily\n",
    "t = np.arange(n)\n",
    "\n",
    "# station coordinates (km), sorted west to east\n",
    "x = np.sort(rng.uniform(low=0, high=60, size=n_stations))\n",
    "y = rng.uniform(low=0, high=30, size=n_stations)\n",
    "\n",
    "def make_anomaly(phi, sd):\n",
    "    # autoregressive anomaly: a[t] = phi * a[t-1] + noise\n",
    "    a = np.zeros(n)\n",
    "    e = rng.normal(loc=0, scale=sd, size=n)\n",
    "    for i in range(1, n):\n",
    "        a[i] = phi * a[i - 1] + e[i]\n",
    "    return a\n",
    "\n",
    "# weather centers and their anomalies\n",
    "centers = rng.uniform(low=[0, 0], high=[60, 30], size=(4, 2))\n",
    "anomalies = np.array([make_anomaly(phi=0.8, sd=1.5) for _ in centers])\n",
    "seasonal = 18 + 5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * (t - 100) / 365)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "id": "83375e9e",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:52:51.332124Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:52:51.331677Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:52:51.598391Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:52:51.596773Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "display_data",
     "metadata": {},
     "data": {
      "text/plain": "<Figure size 600x300 with 1 Axes>",
      "image/png": ""
     }
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3))\n",
    "ax.scatter(x, y, color=\"tab:blue\", s=15, label=\"stations\")\n",
    "ax.scatter(centers[:, 0], centers[:, 1], color=\"tab:red\", marker=\"x\", label=\"weather centers\")\n",
    "ax.set_aspect(\"equal\")\n",
    "ax.set_xlabel(\"X (km)\")\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel(\"Y (km)\")\n",
    "ax.legend(loc=\"upper left\", bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 1), frameon=False)\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "60eb94c9",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Assemble the cluster\n",
    "\n",
    "Instead of an info table, the cluster can also be assembled in memory: set up each `TemperatureSeries` with `.set_data()` and its coordinates, then `.append()` it. Records start at random dates, and some stations have long gaps:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "id": "78634f4d",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:52:51.603106Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:52:51.602603Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:52:52.953992Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:52:52.952737Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Series in the cluster: 40\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "dates = pd.date_range(start=\"2021-01-01\", periods=n, freq=\"D\")\n",
    "tsc = TemperatureSeriesCluster(name=\"Large Network\")\n",
    "\n",
    "for k in range(n_stations):\n",
    "    # mix of weather center anomalies, closer centers weigh more\n",
    "    d = np.hypot(centers[:, 0] - x[k], centers[:, 1] - y[k])\n",
    "    w = np.exp(-d**2 / (2 * 15**2))\n",
    "    values = seasonal + (w / w.sum()) @ anomalies + rng.normal(loc=0, scale=0.8, size=n)\n",
    "\n",
    "    # random record start and some long gaps\n",
    "    values[: rng.integers(low=0, high=300)] = np.nan\n",
    "    if k % 3 == 0:\n",
    "        i_gap = rng.integers(low=300, high=650)\n",
    "        values[i_gap : i_gap + rng.integers(low=20, high=60)] = np.nan\n",
    "\n",
    "    name = f\"ST{k + 1:02d}\"\n",
    "    ts = TemperatureSeries(name=name, alias=name)\n",
    "    ts.set_data(\n",
    "        input_df=pd.DataFrame({\"datetime\": dates, \"T\": values}),\n",
    "        input_dtfield=\"datetime\",\n",
    "        input_varfield=\"T\",\n",
    "    )\n",
    "    ts.x = x[k]\n",
    "    ts.y = y[k]\n",
    "    tsc.append(new_object=ts)\n",
    "\n",
    "tsc.update(details=True)\n",
    "print(f\"Series in the cluster: {len(tsc.catalog)}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "76966940",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Data availability\n",
    "\n",
    "The Gantt chart sizes each row to the space available. With many series the bars become thin lines, and the station labels give way to a series count. The prevalence panel keeps its rows aligned with the Gantt chart, sorted by coverage:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "4800377c",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:52:52.958617Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:52:52.958107Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:52:58.616679Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:52:58.614929Z"
    }

      "image/png": ""
     }
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "tsc.view()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "d4e32514",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The overlapping data panel shows how the network grows during the first year, as stations start recording, and the dips caused by the long gaps."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "c04480fb",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## All series together\n",
    "\n",
    "Above `n_series_max`, the `series` layout draws every station in a light background style, without a legend or mean lines. The overlaid histograms add up to a shading of where values concentrate, and the CDFs show the spread among stations:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 6,
   "id": "89684ffd",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:52:58.621689Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:52:58.621136Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:53:01.435652Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:53:01.434022Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "display_data",
     "metadata": {},
     "data": {
      "text/plain": "<Figure size 1003.94x472.441 with 3 Axes>",
      "image/png": ""
     }
    }
   ],

    "tsc.view_specs[\"layout\"] = \"series\"\n",
    "tsc.view()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "886d9518",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Highlighting stations\n",
    "\n",
    "To follow particular stations, list them in `view_specs[\"highlight\"]`. They are drawn in color, with a legend and mean lines, on top of the others. Lets highlight the westmost and the eastmost stations:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 7,
   "id": "c39f66b7",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:53:01.440536Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:53:01.440029Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:53:04.361513Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:53:04.359976Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "display_data",
     "metadata": {},
     "data": {
      "text/plain": "<Figure size 1003.94x472.441 with 3 Axes>",
      "image/png": ""
     }
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "tsc.view_specs[\"highlight\"] = [\"ST01\", \"ST40\"]\n",
    "tsc.view()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "1ec5454b",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Highlighting also works on small clusters, to point out one station among the others. To clear it, set it back to `None`."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "22195609",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Correlation between many stations\n",
    "\n",
    "The `correlation` layout also drops labels and value annotations above `n_series_max`:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 8,
   "id": "3f006ee8",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:53:04.366592Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:53:04.366058Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:53:05.089439Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:53:05.087656Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "display_data",
     "metadata": {},
     "data": {
      "text/plain": "<Figure size 478.346x472.441 with 2 Axes>",
      "image/png": ""
     }
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "tsc.view_specs[\"highlight\"] = None\n",
    "tsc.view_specs[\"layout\"] = \"correlation\"\n",
    "tsc.view()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "ada4c686",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "All stations correlate strongly, so the default color range (-1 to 1) hides the structure. Narrow it with `range_corr`. Since stations are named from west to east, the heatmap now reads as a map of how correlation changes along the region, highest near the diagonal (neighbors):"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 9,
   "id": "7f495781",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:53:05.094093Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:53:05.093574Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:53:05.821856Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:53:05.820384Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "display_data",
     "metadata": {},
     "data": {
      "text/plain": "<Figure size 478.346x472.441 with 2 Axes>",
      "image/png": ""
     }
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "tsc.view_specs[\"range_corr\"] = [0.7, 1.0]\n",
    "tsc.view()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "f775781d",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "For many stations, correlation against distance is often more telling. Combine `.get_correlation()` with the station coordinates:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 10,
   "id": "7dd29a35",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:53:05.826670Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:53:05.826164Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:53:06.740375Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:53:06.739750Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "display_data",
     "metadata": {},
     "data": {
      "text/plain": "<Figure size 750x450 with 1 Axes>",
      "image/png": ""
     }
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "df_corr = tsc.get_correlation(method=\"pearson\")\n",
    "names = list(df_corr.index)\n",
    "coords = {name: (tsc.collection[name].x, tsc.collection[name].y) for name in names}\n",
    "\n",
    "ls_dist, ls_corr = [], []\n",
    "for i in range(len(names)):\n",
    "    for j in range(i + 1, len(names)):\n",
    "        (xi, yi), (xj, yj) = coords[names[i]], coords[names[j]]\n",
    "        ls_dist.append(np.hypot(xi - xj, yi - yj))\n",
    "        ls_corr.append(df_corr.iloc[i, j])\n",
    "\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3))\n",
    "ax.scatter(ls_dist, ls_corr, s=4, color=\"tab:blue\", alpha=0.5)\n",
    "ax.set_xlabel(\"Distance (km)\")\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel(\"Pearson r\")\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "cab006ff",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Correlation decays with distance, as nearby stations share more weather. This is the reason why inverse distance weighting works well in `.regionalize()`."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "ee4f5a13",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Recap\n",
    "\n",
    "- Above `view_specs[\"n_series_max\"]` series, the cluster views drop per-series labels and colors.\n",
    "- The Gantt chart fits its rows to the space available, turning into lines for many series.\n",
    "- `view_specs[\"highlight\"]` draws selected stations in color over the others.\n",
    "- For many stations, correlation against distance complements the heatmap."
   ]
  }
